name: December 7, 2022 Regular Meeting
agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-
19 and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s Order (revised
September 22, 2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote,
and the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be
live streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to mlinden@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. You must first sign up to speak before the item you would like
to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference to be
recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak and
downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings
As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency, as well as states of
emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, State of California, and a federal emergency
declared by the President of the United States. In order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the Commission
meeting will be open and public but conducted virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to
the health or safety of attendees. This way, the public, the staff, and the Commission will not be physically in the same
place.
The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the
agenda but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the Commission
and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.
Members of the public wishing to speak during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. You must first
sign up to speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the
Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https://MalibuCity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing
up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.
Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the
public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this
meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous
meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any
conditions imposed.
Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an
item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or
abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent
Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent
Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public speakers
shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no final
action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow the
rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the
office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing MLinden@MalibuCity.org.
The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental
Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Frost called the meeting to order at 5:01 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Chris Frost; Vice Chair Doug Stewart; Commissioners Keegan Gibbs
  and Joshua Spiegel; and Ex Officio Member Brent Woodworth

  ABSENT:  Commissioner Daphne Anneet

  ALSO PRESENT:  Susan Dueñas, Public Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works
  Director; Luis Flores, Public Safety Liaison; Gabe Etcheverry, Fire Safety Liaison; Greg
  Hisel, Fire Safety Liaison; Brad Yocum, Fire Safety Liaison; Arthur Aladjadjian, Public
  Works Superintendent; Parker Davis, Media Technician; Lieutenant Dustin Carr, Los
  Angeles County Sheriff’s Department; and Mary Linden, Executive Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Gibbs moved, and Commissioner Spiegel seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0,
  Commissioner Anneet absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Executive Assistant Linden reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on October 26, 2022, with the amended agenda posted on October 28, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL / PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Khushi Patel, a student at California Polytechnic Pomona, asked what the Public
  Safety Department did to protect safety at schools.

  Alicia Peak, Parks and Recreation Commissioner and mother, expressed concern
  about safety at Bluffs Park. She stated she was worried about something serious
  happening. She suggested hiring full-time security or a full-time ranger. She stated
  the Sheriff’s Department was not responsive enough.

ITEM 2.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  In response to Ms. Patel, Public Safety Director Dueñas stated that the City does
  not have direct jurisdictional responsibility for safety at the schools., She added that
  the City’s Public Safety Department works with the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
  Department (LASD) and the local school district to ensure safety at local schools.
  She stated the City was contracting for a comprehensive safety assessment to be
  conducted for all Malibu schools. She stated she submitted a proposal to the Santa
  Monica-Malibu Unified School District (SMMUSD) for a temporary impound yard
  at Malibu High School. She stated Carey Upton, SMMUSD Chief Operations
  Officer, stated he would work with the City on using at minimum the upper parking
  lot from Memorial Day to Labor Day. She announced that the City Council declared
  November 9, 2022 as the City’s Day of Remembrance to recognize the devastation
  of the Woolsey Fire and the efforts everyone who helped during the fire. She
  encouraged everyone to honor the day by doing at least one thing to be more
  prepared for a disaster.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores discussed the September homeless outreach report
  from The People Concern. He stated eight people were taken off the street, three of
  whom were placed in permanent housing, one temporarily housed, and one
  Woolsey Fire victim relocated to Santa Barbara. He stated license plate reader
  cameras were expected to be delivered in November. He stated staff were working
  with LASD on locations for installation. He stated responses to the request for
  proposals (RFP) for interim shelter beds for homeless would be presented to the
  City Council on November 28. He stated staff was working with Knox for
  educational materials about the KnoxBox emergency access program. He discussed
  a small fire in October. He stated it was the fourth encampment fire this year, which
  was down from 23 last year.

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry discussed the peak fire season of October through
  December and upcoming weather. He reported Live Fuel Moisture (LFM) levels
  were down to 56 percent. He stated staff were not satisfied with maps provided by
  the Beacon Box vendor, so new maps were provided. He stated eight Beacon Boxes
  were installed, and two were waiting for confirmation from the neighborhood. He
  stated 12 more were received and locations for installation were identified. In
  response to a previous inquiry from Vice Chair Stewart, he discussed how mutual
 Malibu Public Safety Commission

  aid agencies would be informed of where the boxes were and how to use them. He
  discussed the success of the hazardous tree removal grant program. He stated the
  Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA) was receptive to the
  City’s request for additional funding to complete 20 requests not filled by original
  grant.

  In response to Commissioner Gibbs, Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry discussed the
  purchase cost of Beacon Boxes. He stated private purchases could be coordinated.
  He stated the only one installed outside the city limits was in upper Corral Canyon.

  In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Beacon Box maps covered all canyons,
  including many beyond the city limits.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated Public Works maintenance crews were on
  standby for high winds expected in the next few days. He discussed repair of
  tripping hazards by Point Dume School. He stated an arborist was investigating
  trees where roots were lifting sidewalks. He discussed several conversations with
  Caltrans about adding bicycle safety features on PCH, specifically westbound from
  Malibu Canyon Road to the city limits. He stated he talked to Caltrans maintenance
  crews to ensure battery backup systems on all signals were maintained.

ITEM 2.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth discussed on October 4 meeting with Los Angeles
  County Fire and CalFire about community brigades. He stated Chief Maroney
  approved moving to next step to begin developing agreements with the Fire
  Department. He stated he attended at Bravo 69 a demonstration of Chinook
  helicopter rapid response capabilities. He stated he hoped to have another
  demonstration in Malibu.

  Commissioner Gibbs stated the Woolsey Fire changed his life and he hoped to
  continue seeing improvements in the future.

  Commissioner Spiegel thanked Ms. Peak for sharing her concerns about safety at
  the parks. He commended the City for fire safety improvements. He stated similar
  efforts were necessary for other potential disasters, such as earthquakes. He
  discussed Los Angeles County Waterworks District 29 and Las Virgenes Municipal
  Water District connecting water lines up Encinal Canyon. He requested discussion
  of more long-term emergency water resources be on future agendas. He discussed
  complaints about Nixle notifications not coming in as timely as before.

  In response to Commissioner Spiegel, Public Safety Director Dueñas discussed the
  City’s notification and alert posting procedures.

  Commissioner Spiegel requested discussion of safety issues on Westward Road be
  added to an agenda prior to next summer. In response to Commissioner Spiegel,

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated the ALPR cameras would require a simple
  encroachment permit. In response to Commissioner Spiegel, Public Works Director
  DuBoux suggested the Tow Yard Ad Hoc Committee provide as many options as
  possible for a permanent tow yard location.

  In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Public Safety Director Dueñas stated she would
  provide the locations identified by the LASD for ALPR camera installation. Vice
  Chair Stewart suggested confirming cell service availability at the locations. In
  response to Vice Chair Stewart, Public Safety Director Dueñas discussed plans for
  identifying locations for evacuation zone signage. He discussed an individual who
  was camping at Surfrider Beach. He commended Ex Officio Member Woodworth,
  Commissioner Gibbs, and Assistant Fire Chief Smith for their work on fire
  brigades. He suggested the brigades be promoted with community education. He
  agreed with Ms. Peak about the need for additional protection at parks. He agreed
  with Commissioner Spiegel about increasing earthquake preparation.

  Chair Frost agreed with Ms. Peak and requested the issue of safety at Bluffs Park
  be added to a future agenda.

  CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Commission requested safety and security at Bluffs Park be
  included in a future agenda.

  Chair Frost stated LFM, not Red Flag, determined when individuals would be
  removed from the brush. He stated Sunset Restaurant did not have bollards near its
  outside eating area. He questioned if that area was property permitted. He stated
  Chief Maroney discussed how brigades could help during an earthquake. He
  discussed complaints about party valets without signage or reflective vests. He
  stated very few deputies were in western Malibu to enforce high speed racing. He
  recommended deputies with Lidar guns be deployed there. He discussed
  insufficient enforcement of recreational vehicle (RV) parking on PCH. He
  requested a summary of citations issued.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0,
  Commissioner Anneet absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Public Safety Services Annual Review
  Recommended Action: 1) Review services provided by the County of Los Angeles
  Sheriff’s Department, Fire Department, and Lifeguards, and Malibu Volunteers on
  Patrol (VOP); and 2) Provide a recommendation to the City Council for service
  level adjustments, if appropriate.

  Public Safety Director Dueñas introduced Los Angeles County Fire Department
  Assistant Chief Drew Smith. Assistant Fire Chief Smith presented the Fire
  Department’s report. He discussed mutual assistance provided by and for other
  agencies, including Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD), MRCA, and LASD.
  He discussed regional firefighting resources. He discussed training workshops
  coordinated with LASD on response to a major wildfire. He thanked Ex Officio
  Member Woodworth, Commissioner Gibbs, and Chair Frost for their engagement
  related to the brigades program and discussed how the brigades could be
  coordinated and utilized. He discussed how technological advancements enhanced
  firefighting. He introduced Community Services Liaison Megan Currier.

  Community Services Liaison Currier discussed the NOAA weather radio
  distribution program. She announced three more distribution events, including at
  Malibu City Hall on Saturday, November 12. She stated about 450 radios were
  distributed in Malibu to date. She provided a presentation of the ZoneHaven
  evacuation zone project, which went live in the Santa Monica Mountains area on
  October 25 at www.community.ZoneHaven.com. She stated staff was working on
  a Know Your Zone campaign. She stated the zones in Malibu changed very slightly
  except for the zone names. She explained the naming convention and how the maps
  would notate areas under evacuation. She displayed how a resident could find their
  zone by address and the information provided. In response to Vice Chair Stewart,
  Community Services Liaison Currier stated there was no ZoneHaven app.

  Assistant Fire Chief Smith discussed how fire risk information was shared with the
  City. Vice Chair Stewart asked if a third paramedic unit in Malibu was possible,
  especially when there were large numbers of visitors. Assistant Fire Chief Smith
  explained that paramedic aircraft were available just outside Malibu. He stated the
  Fire Department had the ability to move equipment to meet a need. He stated large
  events were often required to have emergency medical services in place. He
  discussed his request for additional coverage in Malibu, including a larger station
 Malibu Public Safety Commission

  to replace Station 88. He stated paramedic service was also available through the
  Lifeguards. He discussed how services could be brought in due to a surge.

  Assistant Fire Chief Smith introduced Lifeguard Chief Dan Murphy who presented
  the report for the Lifeguards. He stated there was more flexibility within the
  Lifeguard coverage. He stated many Lifeguards were expanding into incident
  management to assist the Fire Department.

  Commissioner Spiegel asked if there was anything the City could do to assist the
  Lifeguards. Lifeguard Chief Murphy stated the City has been a longtime partner
  and its support was appreciated. He stated the Lifeguards could use a paramedic
  assessment unit such as what is used in Hermosa Beach.

  Assistant Fire Chief Smith stated the Fire Department discussed augmented
  services provided in other cities for large events. He stated the costs would be billed
  to the City, which could then pass those costs to the event organizers. In response
  to Commissioner Gibbs, Assistant Fire Chief Smith stated it could be done in
  Malibu through a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). Commissioner Gibbs
  suggested it be considered as a requirement for a major event permit. Public Safety
  Director Dueñas stated it could be considered as part of a special event permit.

  In response to Commissioner Gibbs, Captain Murphy discussed additional
  resources paid for by the organizers of the Malibu Triathlon.

  Lieutenant Carr provided a presentation for the Sheriff’s Department’s annual
  report and the 2022 Summer Beach Enforcement Operation. He discussed the
  impact of staff retirements and turnover on Beach Team statistics. He stated LASD
  may pre-hire from other jurisdictions in the future.

  In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Lieutenant Carr stated both deputies and the
  VOP issue parking citations in the beach parking lots and along PCH. In response
  to Vice Chair Stewart, he stated the statistics did not include VOP citation numbers.

  Chair Frost suggested the Beach Team utilize the electronic ticket writers provided
  by the City as often as possible.

  Commissioner Spiegel discussed the City’s cost to provide the Beach Team that
  was enforcing areas not in the City’s jurisdiction. He stated he expected far more
  vehicles to be towed to the temporary tow yard. Lieutenant Carr stated traffic
  citations were moving violations issued on PCH, not in the beach lots.

  Vice Chair Stewart stated the City spent approximately $900,000 for the Beach
  Team and received about $200,000 to $300,000 through its percentage of fine
  revenue. In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Lieutenant Carr discussed the transport
  procedures required for arrests. He stated arrests in Malibu accounted for about
  one-third of the Lost Hills Station’s arrest totals. Vice Chair Stewart stated the

  deployment of the Beach Team deputies should be evaluated. Lieutenant Carr
  stated they spent a significant amount of time on the beach.

  In response to Commissioner Gibbs, Lieutenant Carr stated Beach Team deputies
  had access to patrol vehicles and could respond in the City when necessary, but
  their primary role was enforcement on the beaches.

  Commissioner Spiegel asked how many tickets were written with the electronic
  ticket writers for illegally parked RVs. Lieutenant Carr stated the new third car was
  restaffed this week and provided with electronic ticket writers. He stated they would
  be citing RVs. Lieutenant Carr stated earlier this evening there were 13 RVs
  counted within the city limits. Commissioner Spiegel stated it was important to the
  community and was not being enforced to the level expected by the community.

  Chair Frost discussed a dossier he provided the Lost Hills Station with a two- to
  three-year history of RVs parked in Malibu. He agreed with Commissioner Spiegel
  about the community’s frustration.

  Vice Chair Stewart requested reports of the numbers of citations issued.

  Mark Russo provided a report on the VOP. He stated three members had moved on
  to law enforcement careers. He stated there were three new trainees. He stated 16
  VOP members worked 7,730 hours in the City and issued 18,343 citations with a
  gross fine amount of $1.33 million. He stated the VOP appreciated the City’s
  support and funding. He stated VOP issued 354 red tags for notice to move. He
  stated they responded to 192 incidents with law enforcement or fire, including
  traffic accidents and assisted law enforcement with 108 tows. He stated the VOP
  team had a strong relationship with deputies and the Lost Hills Station.

  In response to Chair Frost, Mr. Russo stated the City signed the revised agreement
  for the new VOP car, and the bailment agreement had been approved. Chair Frost
  commended the VOP for an amazing job. In response to Chair Frost, Mr. Russo
  discussed the history of the VOP program.

  B.  2022 Summer Beach Enforcement Operation Summary
  Recommended Action: Receive and file summary report of the 2022 Summer
  Beach Enforcement Operation.

  Item No. 5.B. was heard concurrently with Item No. 5.A.

  C.  Public Safety Agency Activity
  Recommended Action: Discuss recent Public Safety Agency activities and receive

  Item No. 5.C. was heard concurrently with Item No. 5.A.

  D.  Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA) Malibu Lower-Cost
  Accommodations Public Works Plan
  Recommended Action: Provide a recommendation to the City Council regarding
  the City’s responsive comments to the MRCA Malibu Lower-Cost
  Accommodations Public Works Plan.

  Public Works Director DuBoux presented the report and provided a description of
  the proposed project.

  Vice Chair Stewart stated most of the Bluffs site was in an environmentally
  sensitive habitat area (ESHA). He stated the land was better used as open space. He
  questioned how they could provide a septic system for 450 people next to ESHA.
  He expressed concern about evacuations. He stated one ranger for over 450 people
  was inefficient. He stated trails on the map did not match the existing trails. He
  noted that the Ramirez Canyon site was outside the city limits. He questioned the
  reason for allowing camping in a residential area. He asked if the City had any
  oversight. In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Public Works Director DuBoux stated
  the Bluffs location was within the septic prohibition area.

  Commissioner Spiegel stated MRCA left Charmlee Park in shambles after the swap
  with the City. He stated campers were going to light fires. He stated he was
  mortified that they would build campgrounds without resources to manage them.
  He stated he hoped the City’s Planning and Public Works Departments made
  MRCA jump through every possible hoop. He stated the Plan was not specific
  enough.

  Public Works Director DuBoux requested the Commission provide specific
  concerns about what the plan proposed.

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth agreed with Vice Chair Stewart and Commissioner
  Spiegel. He stated the Plan was a fire disaster waiting to happen. He stated the
  facilities could be a attractive nuisance to homeless individuals. He stated too much
  was being crammed into too few acres.

  Commissioner Gibbs discussed Leo Carrillo State Beach where open flame fires
  were permitted but not during Red Flags. He expressed doubt that MRCA would
  adequately staff and manage the properties in the same way Leo Carrillo was staffed
  and managed.

  Chair Frost agreed with Commissioner Gibbs. He stated he doubted MRCA would
  manage it properly based on its past management record. He discussed a fire that
  began in Bluffs Park and went downhill and destroyed nine homes on Malibu Road.

  Commissioner Spiegel stated fire rings did a great job of managing flames. He
  expressed concern about the safety of twig fires started in flameless sites.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission

  Vice Chair Stewart stated the campgrounds would result in an overnight five
  percent increase in Malibu population.

  Commissioner Spiegel asked if MRCA rangers would be on roving patrols.

MOTION  Chair Frost moved, and Commissioner Spiegel seconded a motion to provide a
  recommendation to the City Council that the following concerns and suggestions
  be included in the City’s comments presented to MRCA in response to its Malibu
  Lower-Cost Accommodations Public Works Plan:

  •  Fires every day with no one there to ensure it did not happen and did not get
  out of control.
  •  Ranger residence needed to include minimum number of rangers per
  number of campers.
  •  Will the kitchen and food preparation areas be properly maintained.
  •  Facilities could become an attractive nuisance to late night homeless
  individuals.
  •  Must include strong evacuation plan for both properties that meets City’s
  requirements and should include regular testing of the plan.
  •  City’s Ordinance prohibiting camping when Life Fuel Moisture reaches a
  specific minimum level should close the campground.
  •  Consider increasing citation fines for violations of the City’s campfire
  ordinance
  •  Can the City label the property a nuisance in response to multiple violations
  of City ordinances in accordance with the City’s nuisance ordinance.
  •  Allow City inspection of the property at any time for compliance with City
  ordinances and the CDP.
  •  Determine an appropriate number of rangers per campers as part of the
  CDP.
  •  Are there sufficient parking spaces for the number of MRCA rangers and
  staff.
  •  How is MRCA going to ensure campers will not walk through ESHA
  •  Campgrounds will be significant strain on City public safety resources
  •  Include all reasonably available technologies in order to rapidly identify
  fires on the property, such as an alert siren or automatic sprinkler system, to
  be shared with the City and local public safety agencies
  •  Specify that that flameless facilities include prohibiting camp stoves
  •  All electrical outlets must be ground fault interrupted (GFI) devices

  The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Commissioner Anneet absent.

Date prepared:  November 17, 2022  Meeting date: December 7, 2022

Subject:  CERT Team Preparedness Activities

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file a report regarding CERT Team
preparedness activities and provide feedback to staff.

DISCUSSION:  In preparation for peak fire season, as well as other potential disasters,
the Malibu CERT Team (CERT Team) in conjunction with the Public Safety Department,
has been upgrading equipment and emergency capabilities.

During the 2018 Woolsey Fire, the telecommunications infrastructure system was
damaged and inoperable, leaving most people who were still in the City with little to no
means to send or receive calls, texts, or information over the cellular networks. In
response, the Malibu CERT Team has been working to fill in this gap, as well as preparing
to respond to other needs of the community in the event of a disaster such as a wildfire or
earthquake.

The Malibu CERT Team Leader (Team Leader) conducted extensive research on satellite
internet options, limitations, and current providers to determine which system would work
best for the locations and needs of the City’s emergency bins. In June, the City purchased
three satellite dishes and three commercial lines to prepare for fire season. One dish
system will be in the Zuma bin to be set up and deployed as necessary, one dish system
will be permanently mounted to the bin located at City Hall, and the third will be kept in

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item 5.A.
 reserve as a mobile unit. When fully set up and connected to the satellites, the system
provides full wireless internet access to residents. The system purchased has multiple
gateways so if the local gateway service is interrupted or damaged, the company can
switch to another one to ensure little to no interruption of service.

In addition to the internet service provided by the company, the City purchased the ability
to have a voice-over-internet-protocol (VOIP) telephone line. Residents will be able to use
the phone at the bin to call emergency contacts to let them know they are safe.
Additionally, this ensures that, should an emergency arise at the bin, the CERT Team will
be able to call 9-1-1 for help if traditional networks and phone lines are inoperable.

The CERT Team has also been working to ensure all City-owned emergency bins will
have power during an extended activation such as an earthquake or fire. Each bin has or
will have solar panels and a battery storage system that will be able to power the above-
mentioned satellite system, the City’s two-way radio and other communications
equipment, and other smaller electric emergency and comfort equipment such as USB
charging stations and LED lighting.

The City also purchased a shelf-stable, five-year lifespan emergency food bar that could
be distributed to residents during an extended event to supplement the residents’ own
emergency food supplies. The CERT Team will be distributing a set quantity of bars to all
the bins with a larger portion going to known gathering locations such as Point Dume
School and Zuma Beach. The CERT Team is also cleaning, refurbishing, and resupplying
emergency bins throughout the City. The objective is to have all emergency bins supplied
with the same items and in a similar format.

During its meeting on October 12, 2022, the CERT Team ran an emergency drill to practice
one of the team’s critical response capabilities – setting up and managing a point of
distribution (POD) and point of information (POI). When activated during a disaster, the
emergency bins may become a POD. Each bin contains a limited amount of basic supplies
to augment residents’ own supplies. The CERT team will be activated to open a POD or
POI at the direction of the City Manager or their designee. When staff cannot reach the
CERT Team to activate them, they will follow the City’s Standard Operating Procedures.

Lastly, the City purchased an additional shipping container to be placed in the Zuma Beach
parking lot to support donation management. During the Woolsey Fire, donations arrived
at Zuma in large quantities. The CERT Team did its best to ensure that the donations were
managed and stored safely, but with no way to secure the items, this proved difficult. To
prevent this from happening in the future, the second shipping container will be lined with
shelves and will largely stand empty and ready to receive and distribute incoming
donations during the next large-scale disaster.

  5:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Frost called the meeting to order at 5:02 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Chris Frost; Vice Chair Doug Stewart; Commissioners Daphne Anneet,
  Keegan Gibbs, and Joshua Spiegel; and Ex Officio Member Brent Woodworth

  ALSO PRESENT:  Susan Dueflas, Public Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works
  Director; Luis Flores, Public Safety Liaison; Gabe Etcheverry, Fire Safety Liaison; Brad
  Yocum, Fire Safety Liaison; Sarah Kaplan, Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan;
  Arthur Aladjadjian, Public Works Superintendent; Parker Davis, Media Technician;
  Lieutenant Dustin Carr, Los Angeles County Sheriffs Department; and Mary Linden,
  Executive Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Executive Assistant Linden reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted

ITEM 2.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Safety Director Dueflas announced the resignation of Fire Safety Liaison
  Greg Hisel. She stated she followed up with Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School
  District (SMMUSD) on her request for an update on using the high school parking
  lot for a tow lot. She discussed a tabletop exercise scheduled in January that will
  focus on earthquakes and infrastructure, particularly serious infrastructure outside
  Malibu that, if damaged, would influence the City.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores stated the City was proceeding with securing three
  interim shelter beds. He announced the next County homeless count was scheduled
  on Wednesday, January 25, 2023. He discussed work to clear two encampments at
  Surfrider Beach. He stated staff was working with the vendor on Knox Box
  educational materials.

  In response to Chair Frost, Public Safety Liaison Flores stated Los Angeles County
  Beaches and Harbors was coordinating with the Sheriffs Department about the two
  individuals encamped at Surfrider Beach.

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry stated there had been very few fires during this
  year’s Red Flag season. He stated Live Fuel Moisture (LFM) was up to 76 percent.
  He stated hazard tree removal was continuing and he expected to work two days
  per week in January. He stated 10 Beacon Boxes should be installed by noon
  tomorrow. He discussed public messaging about fire safety during the holidays.

  Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan stated the City was updating the
  Emergency Operations Center (EOC) and conducting EOC training for City staff.
  She discussed staff training on the City’s mass disaster notification system.

  Public Works Director DuBoux discussed weather information provided by the
  City’s weather forecasting consultant. He stated there had been no incidents in
  recent rainstorms.

ITEM 2.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth congratulated Vice Chair Stewart on his election
  to City Council. He commended Public Safety Director Dueflas and Emergency
  Services Coordinator Kaplan on their work with the EOC. He expressed interest in
  participating in the tabletop exercise in January. He discussed funding obtained
  from Malibu Foundation for fire brigade communications equipment.

  Commissioner Anneet commended the work of the CERT team. She expressed
  gratitude for the safety and security of living in a community where she was able
  to live freely without fear of retribution. She expressed concern for the women of
  Iran.

  In response to Commissioner Spiegel, Public Safety Liaison Flores discussed the
  timeline of the Beacon Boxes. He stated the vendor advised it was a shipping delay.

  Vice Chair Stewart agreed with Commissioner Spiegel’s disappointment with the
  Beacon Box vendor. He commended Public Safety Director Dueñas for getting the
  antenna for eastern Malibu moving along. He discussed a Sheriff’s Relief
  Association website set up for Sheriff cadets and recruits impacted by the recent
  tragedy. He thanked all the Commissioners for working with him over the years.
  He commended Chair Frost for his many years of service and for his mentorship.
  He thanked staff, Arson Watch, CERT and the Volunteers on Patrol (VOP).

  Chair Frost stated it was wonderful working with this Commission. He commended
  Commissioner Spiegel on his award from the Board of Realtors. He stated ticketing
  was impacting the number of illegally parked vehicles. He commended Lieutenant
  Carr. He agreed with Commissioner Spiegel’s concerns about the camera delays.
  He stated the Commission should revisit the locations selected for the cameras. He
  commended Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan for setting up the EOC. He
  stated the antenna at Bluffs Park would have been done sooner if Public Safety
  Director Duefias had been in charge of it. Chair Frost discussed a fundraiser that
  benefited the Sheriff cadets impacted by the tragedy. He commended emergency
  room doctors and nurses who tended to the victims.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  CERT Team Preparedness Activities
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report regarding CERT Team
  preparedness activities and provide feedback to staff.

  Richard Garvey, CERT Team Leader, presented the report. He discussed
  communication problems during major emergencies like the Woolsey Fire. He
  discussed the need for reliable power sources, particularly at City Hall and Zuma
  Beach. He discussed solar panels added at City Hall and to be added at Zuma Beach,
  which would allow for basic services, such as charging devices and providing
  lighting and power for communication systems used by CERT and the City. He
  discussed satellite communication options. He stated Voice Over Internet Protocol
  (VoiP) phone service would also be available. He stated satellite service allowed
  transmission of information between locations. He discussed HughesNet, the
  satellite provider.

  Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan discussed zone aware sites. Mr. Garvey
  stated ZoneHaven could be viewed and streamed live from the supply bins.

  Mr. Garvey stated a new container had been ordered for acceptance of donations at
  Zuma Beach. He discussed food and water resources stored in emergency bins. He
  stated CERT was working to stock all bins identically.

  Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan thanked Mr. Garvey for his work.

  Chair Frost commended Mr. Garvey and the CERT Team. He stated residents
  should not rely on the City and CERT for all of their food and water needs.

  Commissioner Anneet thanked Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan and Mr.
  Garvey. She stated she felt more secure afier hearing that report. She asked about
  the criteria for activating Wi-Fi at Zuma Beach. Mr. Garvey stated an emergency
  declaration would be the first step. He stated activating it during an extended public
  safety power shutoff (PSPS) was being discussed. Commissioner Anneet stated that
  would be extremely helpful to the community during a PSPS. Public Safety
  Director Dueñas stated it could definitely be activated during a prolonged PSPS.

  Commissioner Spiegel thanked Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan and Mr.
  Garvey. He expressed concern that most of the community was woefully
  unprepared.

  In response to Commissioner Spiegel, Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan
  discussed emergency preparedness community education. She stated having a
  minimum of two to three week supply of food and water was strongly emphasized
  at every training session.

  B.  Mid-Year Report to the City Council
  Recommended Action: Develop a list of Commission activities for the period of
  July through December 2022 to be included in the City Manager’s Mid-Year
  Commission Activity Report, scheduled to be presented to the City Council at its
  Regular meeting on January 23, 2023.

  Executive Assistant Linden presented the report.

MOTION  Chair Frost moved and Commissioner Gibbs seconded a motion to submit the list
  of Commission activities for the period of July through December 2022 prepared
  by staff to be included in the City Manager’s Mid-Year Commission Activity
  Report. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  C.  Public Safety Agency Activity
  Recommended Action: Discuss recent Public Safety Agency activities and receive
  and file activity reports from the County of Los Angeles Sheriff’s Department, Fire
  Department, and Lifeguard Division.

  Lieutenant Carr thanked everyone for their support of the cadets impacted by the
  recent tragedy. He thanked Chair Frost for acknowledging progress being made
  with parking tickets. He reported that 41 citations were issued for oversized
  vehicles, many of which were in the $500 fine range. He discussed arrests for
  drinking in public at Legacy Park. He stated problems at Bluffs Park, including
  illegally parked recreational vehicles, had been addressed.

  Vice Chair Stewart discussed comments from a Parks and Recreation
  Commissioner at the last Public Safety Commission meeting about individuals at
  Bluffs Park on weekends and afternoons when children were present.

  Public Works Director DuBoux wished everyone a safe and happy holiday.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 6:23 p.m., Chair Frost moved and Commissioner Anneet seconded a motion to
  adjourn. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.
